hospital_course: You came in with worsening shortness of breath, more cough, and more mucus than usual. You received steroids, breathing treatments, and oxygen. Your breathing has improved and you no longer need oxygen at rest.

medications.name: Prednisone
medications.note: Then stop. Do not stop it early.

medications.name: Albuterol inhaler (Ventolin HFA)
medications.note: Use it for wheezing or shortness of breath.

medications.name: Tiotropium (Spiriva HandiHaler)
medications.note: Inhale the capsule powder with the HandiHaler device. Do not swallow the capsule.

diet: Eat smaller meals more often if you feel short of breath when full.
Drink fluids to keep mucus thin unless told otherwise.
activity: Walk a little more each day, resting when you need to. Try pursed-lip breathing during activity.
Do not smoke. Avoid smoke, strong fumes, and very cold air.
care: Rinse your mouth with water after using the Spiriva HandiHaler.
Keep a list of how many puffs of albuterol you use each day.
monitoring: Count how often you use your albuterol inhaler each day for 7 days and bring the list to your visit.
Check your temperature every evening for 7 days.

follow_up.purpose: a flare-up follow-up and an inhaler technique check
an intake visit for a breathing exercise program

warning_signs: severe trouble breathing or you cannot speak in full sentences
blue or gray lips or fingertips
call_clinic: you need albuterol more often than every 4 hours
your mucus turns green or bloody
a fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher
